findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "dev" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: package_check, packages_check, web_extract, web_fetch, web_contents, web_search · Private data: package_docs, web_extract, web_fetch, document_to_markdown, extract_tables · Public sink: web_extract, web_contents, web_search, extract_tables.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: package_check, packages_check, web_extract, web_fetch, web_contents, web_search · Private data: package_docs, web_extract, web_fetch, document_to_markdown, extract_tables · Public sink: web_extract, web_contents, web_search, extract_tables

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

remediation.title: Tool description changed since last scan
remediation.detail: Tool "example_output" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
